```artifact
Feature: Patient Management System - Register, Update, and Delete Patient Details

  Background:
    Given the Patient Management System is operational
    And the current date is within the last three years

  Scenario: Register a new Patient
    When a user attempts to register a new Patient
    Then the system should allow the registration
    And create a new Patient record

  Scenario: View and Update Existing Patient Details
    Given a user has registered a Patient
    When the user views and updates the Patient details
    Then the latest details should be displayed and saved
    And any previous details should be discarded

  Scenario: Delete Patient Details with Consultation Requests
    Given a user has registered a Patient with Consultation Requests in the last three years
    When the user attempts to delete the Patient details
    Then the system should deny the deletion
    And prompt the user about the Consultation Requests

  Scenario: Rollback by a Month
    Given a user has made changes to the Patient details
    When the user chooses to rollback by a month
    Then the system should restore the previous month' extraneous details

  Scenario: Restore Backup on Dummy Production System
    Given a backup is created
    When the backup is restored on a dummy production system
    And the dummy production system is purged
    Then the system should verify the completeness and correctness of the backup

  Scenario: Dummy Production System Maintenance
    Given the dummy production system is located in Mangalore HQ
    And it is stored in a fireproof cabinet 25 KM away from the Hospital
    When the dummy production system is accessed for restoration
    Then the system should ensure the backup is intact and ready for use
```

Note: The JSON objects have been designed to match the Gherkin artifact structure, with IDs corresponding to the scenarios. The "expected" fields contain concrete, checkable outcomes based on the requirements provided. The "kind" field indicates whether the test is a positive scenario (expected to succeed under normal conditions), negative (expected to fail or raise an error), or boundary (testing at the limits). The "preconditions" field sets the initial state before each test, and the "steps" field outlines the actions taken during the test. The "expected" field reflects the specific system state or variable that should be asserted after the test steps are executed. The "id" field links the JSON test case to the corresponding requirement in the Gherkin artifact.

This test suite covers the functional requirements and constraints specified, with scenarios designed to test the normal operation, error handling, and boundary conditions. It also includes negative test cases to ensure the system correctly handles attempts to delete patients with recent consultation requests. The dummy production system maintenance scenario ensures the system can restore and verify backups, and the location and security of the dummy system are tested. The suite is grounded, with concrete values and expected outcomes derived from the requirement text, ensuring syntactic validity and oracle assertiveness.
